description.narrative:
The main purpose of the first phase of activities was to convene actors in-person and virtually and to establish two active learning trajectories: a learning trajectory on “strengthening community seed banks” and a learning trajectory on “improving the integration of crop varieties adapted to small-scale farmers’ needs into national frameworks, policy and planning”, with agreed rules of engagement for each.
Members of the Community of Practice (CoP), established in Harare, Zimbabwe in 2024 , met in Manila, the Philippines on 14-15 September 2025, ahead of the second Farmers’ Rights Symposium. In Manila, sixty individuals convened from Africa, Asia, and Europe, including members of the BSF CoP, to share knowledge and experiences of national seed policies and legislation and best practices pertaining to community seed banks, reflecting diverse approaches to implementing measures to strengthen and support FMSS. A second day was dedicated towards establishing the vision, the narrative, and the strategy ofthe CoP. In a series of collaborative sessions, members formulated their ideas and expectations about the identity of the CoP and concluded with the synthesis of key policy recommendations developed from the outcomes of Harare. The CoP took these recommendations forward during the 11th Governing Body meeting in Peru, November 2025, presented during a side event titled 'Exploring Policies to Promote and Strengthen Farmer-Managed Seed Systems'.
The in-person and virtual meetings during phase one resulted in two knowledge and learning roadmaps (one per trajectory). In addition, phase one aimed to contributed to the ongoing African Union process to develop a framework, strategy and action plan for farmer-managed seed systems on the continent. Altogether, the activities, learnings and outputs of phase one have formed the basis for the three learning trajectories that will be pursued under this second LoA. These are:
- Learning trajectory 1: Strengthening Community Seed Banks Community seed banks (CSBs)can serve multiple functions, conserving and safeguarding agrobiodiversity at the community and local level and providing communities with access to affordable, locally adapted, and diverse varieties. CSBs are also increasingly being recognised for theirpotential in bridging the gap between ex-situ and in-situ conservation, facilitating the exchange of genetic material for conservation and development through participatory research and breeding programmes. The CoP membersdiscussed the need to systematically document practical lessons, innovations, and bottlenecks in seed conservation and exchange systems, as well as a comparative analysis of different monitoring and evaluation approaches of CSBs that incorporate farmer and community-relevant indicators. Increasing institutional support and interlinkages with gene banks, on the national and international scale, was also identified as critical to strengthening CSBs.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
